grades.quote: when the access address is not naturally aligned, if the hardware implementation supports nonaligned access and the current computing environment is configured to allow non-aligned access, then the non-alignment exception will not be triggered; otherwise, the non-alignment exception will be triggered.
grades.reason: Directly explains the hardware and environment conditions determining whether a misaligned access triggers an exception.

grades.quote: An EEI may not guarantee misaligned loads and stores are handled invisibly. In this case, loads and stores that are not naturally aligned may either complete execution successfully or raise an exception. The exception raised can be either an address-misaligned exception or an access-fault exception.
grades.reason: Directly identifies successful execution and possible exceptions; also discusses trap handling, slow execution, and lack of guaranteed atomicity.

grades.quote: FLH and FSH are only guaranteed to execute atomically if the effective address is naturally aligned.
grades.reason: Provides the useful atomicity consequence, but does not describe whether misaligned accesses complete or trap.

grades.quote: As described in Section 2.6, the execution environment defines whether misaligned floating-point loads and stores are handled invisibly or raise a contained or fatal trap.
grades.reason: Directly explains invisible handling versus contained or fatal traps, and also addresses atomicity.
